meta.institution: KJSIT (K J Somaiya Institute of Technology, formerly KJSIEIT)
meta.basis: Gap analysis performed after reading all 405 pages of all 12 fetched handbook documents plus two official-site supplements, and after inspecting the existing Neo4j graph.
meta.rule: A topic is only listed as MISSING here if it was searched for across the whole corpus and not found. Recommended sources are real, official KJSIT/Somaiya pages; none are invented.

broken_or_absent_links.detail: The handbook page lists 'HR Policies' as an <li> with no <a> element at all - not a broken URL, no link is rendered. Verified in the page HTML, not just visually.
broken_or_absent_links.resolution: Chapter 4 HUMAN RESOURCE POLICIES (39 pages) of the 2018 Second Publication was located and fully ingested. Probing the 2022 folder for a chapter-04 filename returned HTTP 403 for every candidate name; no HR policy PDF was found anywhere on kjsit.somaiya.edu.in.
broken_or_absent_links.conclusion: The HR policy EXISTS but its current version is unpublished. Do not conclude it does not exist.

broken_or_absent_links.detail: href is literally '---'. The 2018 Second Publication link works.
broken_or_absent_links.resolution: Recorded as unavailable. The 2018 edition supersedes it anyway.

broken_or_absent_links.detail: The 2022 chapter files are numbered 01,02,03,05,06,07,08,09,10,11,12. There is no 04. In the 2018 edition, chapter 4 is HUMAN RESOURCE POLICIES.
broken_or_absent_links.resolution: Consistent with HR Policies having been withheld from the 2022 republication.

incomplete_documents.detail: The PDF is 5 pages. Its own running footer reads 'Examination Manual Part I/V.01_21 ... 7 of 54'. Only pages 0-7 of a 54-page Examination Manual are published, and the text breaks off mid-sentence after the PG grade table.
incomplete_documents.missing: 47 pages: everything on revaluation, supplementary examinations, malpractice, ATKT, progression, SGPI/CGPI computation and examination conduct under CBCGS Scheme I.
incomplete_documents.partially_resolved_by: https://kjsit-files.somaiya.edu.in/Examinations/Exam+Cell+Website+Data.pdf (22 pages, current, Scheme III) found on the official Examinations page during cross-check. It covers attendance, progression, grace marks, condonation and malpractice, but is NOT the 54-page manual.
incomplete_documents.recommended_source: The complete 'Examination Manual (Examination / Evaluation Guidelines) for Undergraduate & Post-Graduate Programs' Parts I-V from the KJSIT Examination Cell.

incomplete_documents.document: 12. Quality Management System Including Accreditation Policies.pdf
incomplete_documents.detail: Pages 19-34 are 15 full-page scanned images with no text layer (page 24 is blank). Naive text extraction returns only the 22-character running header and would silently drop the entire annexure.
incomplete_documents.resolution: The embedded images were extracted from the nested Form XObjects and read visually. They are the signed 15-page 'Revised Higher Studies Policy of KJSIEIT' (PhD sponsorship, study leave, bonds, penalties, incentives), dated 22/12/2021. Fully ingested as 23 provisions.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Attendance is the single most common cause of a student being barred from an examination. The 75% rule is published; the escape valve is not.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: The 75% minimum attendance requirement and the defaulter consequence ARE published (handbook Examination Policy p3; Exam Cell data p7). What is absent everywhere in the corpus is any condonation procedure, medical-grounds exemption, authority who may grant it, application form, deadline, or appeal route. The only condonation in the corpus is Ordinance O.5045 condonation of MARKS, which is a different thing.
questions_unanswerable: Can my attendance shortfall be condoned?
What is the medical exemption procedure?
Who approves attendance condonation?
What documents do I submit for a medical exemption?
Can I appeal a defaulter declaration?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT Examination Cell / Dean Academics - the complete Examination Manual Parts I-V, and any Academic Council resolution on attendance condonation.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Students who withdraw, transfer or cancel admission need to know what is refundable and by when.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: Handbook section 5.1.7 covers only how fees are determined and collected. No refund schedule, no cancellation rule, no deadline. The only refund-adjacent rule in the corpus is that the Rs. 500 provisional-admission fee pending revaluation is not refunded.
questions_unanswerable: What is refundable if I cancel my admission?
Is there a refund deadline?
What happens to my fees if I transfer?
missing_policies.recommended_source: Fees Regulating Authority (FRA) / Shikshan Shulka Samiti refund rules as adopted by KJSIT, and the KJSIT Accounts Section.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Date questions are among the most frequent a student assistant receives.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: The handbook explains how the academic calendar is prepared and displayed but contains no dates, no semester boundaries, no examination dates, and no holiday list. HR section 4.21 defers the holiday list entirely to University circulars.
questions_unanswerable: When does the semester start?
What are this year's holidays?
When are the term tests?
missing_policies.recommended_source: https://kjsit.somaiya.edu.in/en/academic-calendar - a live page, not a handbook document.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Backlog handling determines whether a student graduates on time.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: A supplementary examination schedule is published for M.Tech Semester I and II only (Exam Cell data, R-PG46). No equivalent rule for B.Tech appears anywhere in the corpus - neither the schedule, the number of attempts, nor the fee.
questions_unanswerable: When is the B.Tech backlog exam?
How many attempts do I get?
What is the backlog exam fee?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT Examination Cell - the complete Examination Manual.

missing_policies.topic: CURRENT REVALUATION / RECHECKING FEE AND WINDOW
missing_policies.why_it_matters: A student deciding whether to apply needs the fee and the deadline.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: The published revaluation procedure (Rs. 500 per subject, Rs. 100 photocopy, 10 working days, 45 day completion) is the University of Mumbai VCD/1 of 2016 procedure from the 2018 edition. The current Exam Cell document replaces the flow with Open House plus an ESE Grievance Form handled by the COE/EEC and states only that 'the student will make necessary payment / rechecking fees' - no amount. Whether the 2018 fees still apply is not established by any current source.
questions_unanswerable: What does revaluation cost now?
What is the deadline to apply now?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT Examination Cell - current rechecking / re-assessment fee notification.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Internship credit requirements affect graduation eligibility.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: Internships appear only as a best-effort placement activity ('if possible', 'provided it does not interfere with attendance') and as an IIIC objective. No internship policy, no duration requirement, no credit rule, no evaluation scheme, no approval process.
questions_unanswerable: How many internship credits do I need?
How long must my internship be?
How is an internship evaluated?
Who approves my internship?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT Dean Academics / Board of Studies - the B.Tech curriculum scheme, which defines PBL and internship credits.

missing_policies.what_is_missing: The Library Manual states Rs. 5 per day for ALUMNI members only, and Rs. 50 for a lost borrower card. No overdue fine rate for regular students, faculty or non-teaching staff, even though Administrative Policies 5.1.5 confirms the Librarian collects fines from students.
questions_unanswerable: What is the library fine per day?
What do I pay for a book returned late?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT Library / Librarian - current circulation fine notification.

missing_policies.topic: ID CARD, LANYARD AND LOST-CARD REPLACEMENT FEES
missing_policies.why_it_matters: The procedure is fully documented but the amount is not, so the answer stops one step short.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: IT Policy 11.1.6 describes the full FIR-and-ticket procedure and says 'the fee to replace a lost ID card is to be paid' without stating it. Same for damaged cards and lanyards. Disciplinary Policy rule 7 likewise says 'on payment of charges'.
questions_unanswerable: How much does a replacement ID card cost?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT Institute Office / ID Card Office.

missing_policies.topic: HOSTEL FEES, MESS CHARGES AND HOSTEL RULES OF CONDUCT
missing_policies.why_it_matters: Hostel eligibility, entry timing (9.00 am - 8.00 pm) and the allotment process ARE published; the money and the discipline rules are not.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: Fees and mess charges are deferred to 'concerned hostel authorities' with no amounts. No hostel code of conduct, leave/outpass rules, or disciplinary procedure.
questions_unanswerable: What does the hostel cost?
What are the hostel discipline rules?
What is the outpass procedure?
missing_policies.recommended_source: Somaiya Trust hostel administration (Somaiya Polytechnic Hostel, Somaiya Management Institute Hostel, Somaiya Medical Hostel).

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Under a Choice Based Credit system, choosing courses is a core student action.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: CBCGS, credits and the credit structure are described, but there is no course registration procedure, no elective selection window, no add/drop rule, and no minimum/maximum credit load per semester.
questions_unanswerable: How do I register for courses?
When do I choose electives?
Can I drop a course?
What is the credit load limit?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT Dean Academics - the complete Examination Manual and the curriculum scheme.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Total credits required is a basic question.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: The minimum credit for M.Tech is published (68 credits). No equivalent total-credit requirement for B.Tech appears anywhere in the corpus.
questions_unanswerable: How many credits do I need to graduate with a B.Tech?
missing_policies.recommended_source: KJSIT B.Tech curriculum scheme approved by the Academic Council.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: Referenced twice as governing student and faculty project IP.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: The IPR Cell that prepares the IPR Policy is described, and the Consultancy Policy states 'the Intellectual Property Policy of the Institute will govern all decisions', but the IPR Policy itself is not published in the handbook.
questions_unanswerable: Who owns my project IP?
How do I file a patent through the institute?

missing_policies.what_is_missing: Student Welfare 9.21 says the Industrial Visit Committee decides 'rules and regulations for Industrial Visit'. Those rules are not in the handbook.
questions_unanswerable: What are the rules for an industrial visit?
Who pays for an industrial visit?

missing_policies.why_it_matters: The Internet Facility Policy (11.7) is written for STAFF only.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: No acceptable-use rule for students' campus internet, other than the digital library rules in the Library Manual. Wi-Fi access rules do cover students.
questions_unanswerable: What am I allowed to do on the campus internet as a student?

missing_policies.why_it_matters: The committee, the squad and the complaint route ARE published.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: The handbook defers punishments entirely to 'AICTE regulations' and 'government guidelines' without reproducing the punishment schedule.
questions_unanswerable: What is the punishment for ragging?
missing_policies.recommended_source: AICTE Notification dated 01-07-2009 on Prevention and Prohibition of Ragging, which the handbook cites.

missing_policies.why_it_matters: A student wants to know how long redressal takes.
missing_policies.what_is_missing: The Internal Grievance Cell procedure says grievances are redressed 'within a reasonable time' and should be 'time bound', without any number. The CWDC sexual-harassment procedure, by contrast, has concrete deadlines (10 working days, 2 weeks, 6 weeks).
questions_unanswerable: How long will my grievance take?

internal_contradictions.detail: Administrative Policies 5.5.1 item 10 says computers should be replaced after every FIVE years. Academic Processes 3.2.6 and Administrative Policies 5.4.4 both say SEVEN years. All three are in the same 2022 edition.
internal_contradictions.handled_as: Both provisions ingested, each flagged with an ambiguity note naming the contradiction.

internal_contradictions.detail: Library circulation table 7.5.4 says Book Bank issues 6 books (one per subject). Value Added Services 7.9 item 7 says 5 books for one semester, for all three schemes.

Academic Processes 3.1.1 states the Institute 'adheres to the curriculum prescribed by University of Mumbai' and refers to 'university Examinations'. The Examination Policy chapter of the same edition, and the current Exam Cell data, describe KJSIT as an autonomous institute running its own CBCGS scheme approved by its own Academic Council.
internal_contradictions.handled_as: Flagged as AMBIGUOUS / REQUIRES VERIFICATION on the affected provision.

internal_contradictions.detail: Academic Processes 3.1.8 says the AVERAGE of both term tests is considered for passing marks. Current Exam Cell data says the TOTAL of both tests is used for B.Tech Scheme III, and the average only for M.Tech Scheme II.
internal_contradictions.handled_as: Flagged; the answer directs the student to the scheme in force for their batch.

internal_contradictions.detail: The revaluation annexure reads 'within twenty (25) working days' - the spelled word and the numeral disagree.
internal_contradictions.handled_as: Flagged; the numeral 25 is used consistently elsewhere in the clause.

internal_contradictions.detail: The depreciation table prints the Air Conditioning Equipments rate as '10' with no percent sign, unlike every other row.
